cards.front: How do you apply the two-second rule to check your following distance?
cards.back: Watch the vehicle ahead pass a checkpoint (such as an overpass or sign post), then count "one thousand and one, one thousand and two." If you reach the checkpoint before finishing the count, your following distance isn't enough — drop back, pick a new checkpoint and count again.

cards.front: What conditions affect driving and require you to increase your following distance beyond the ideal-conditions rule?
cards.back: Road conditions, vehicle conditions, your physical and mental condition, traffic conditions, lighting conditions and weather conditions.

cards.front: What are the risks of driving faster than the traffic flow?
cards.back: You can't maintain a safe following distance, you make more lane changes (each one a quick decision, increasing the chance of a wrong one), and you tire more quickly from tension and mental and physical fatigue.

cards.front: What is a good safety practice when driving slowly up or down a hill?
cards.back: Use your four-way flashers (some companies require this), and always use the right lane when travelling more slowly than other traffic where a passing lane is provided.

cards.front: How can you reduce the size of your danger zone?
cards.back: Slow down — the danger zone shrinks as speed is reduced — and cover the brake pedal with your foot any time you see a potential hazard developing, such as when approaching an intersection.

cards.front: How do conventional, cab-over and forward-control vehicles differ?
cards.back: In a conventional design the driver's seat and steering wheel are behind the steering axle; in a cab-over design the seat is above the steering axle; in a forward-control design the seat is in front of the steering axle. Each changes your viewpoint and where you start your turn.

cards.front: What is a vehicle's turning radius?
cards.back: When a vehicle turns a corner it travels on a curve; if it continued it would drive a complete circle. The distance from the centre of that imaginary circle to the vehicle's wheel is the turning radius. Rear tires have a different turning radius than front tires.

cards.front: What is wheelbase, and how does it relate to off track?
cards.back: Wheelbase is the distance between the front wheels and the rear wheels of a vehicle. Vehicles with longer wheelbases have more off tracking than those with short wheelbases, and a combination vehicle usually has more off tracking than a single-unit vehicle.

cards.front: What is inertia and how does it affect you in a curve?
cards.back: Inertia is the tendency of moving objects to continue moving forward in a straight line. The faster you're going and the heavier your vehicle, the more inertia pushes your vehicle away from the path of the curve.

cards.front: What is traction, and what can happen if you brake in a curve you entered too fast?
cards.back: Traction is the grip created between a vehicle's tires and the road. If you enter a curve too quickly and try to slow down by braking, you may lose traction, causing your vehicle to skid, roll over or jackknife.

cards.front: Where should you position your front wheels when curving to the left?
cards.back: Keep the front wheels close to the right edge of the lane to keep your driver's side rear wheels out of the next lane of traffic.

cards.front: What are the risks of making a right turn with too small a turning arc?
cards.back: Off tracking may cause the trailer's back wheels to scrape the curb or leave the road, crowd cyclists on your right, run over curbs and sidewalks (damaging tires and seriously injuring pedestrians and cyclists), or hit a power pole, sign post or lamp standard.

cards.front: Why should you keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb when turning right?
cards.back: It prevents other drivers from passing you on the right.

cards.front: What steering method is recommended when you need to do a lot of turning?
cards.back: The hand-over-hand method — pull on the right half of the wheel for right turns and the left half for left turns. Don't grasp the inside of the steering wheel; if it slips or jerks you may injure yourself. Always use both hands.

cards.front: What are the four rules for driving through a traffic circle or roundabout?
cards.back: Slow down as you approach; yield to any traffic in the circle; if another vehicle arrives at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right; go around the circle to the right (counter-clockwise).

cards.front: How do traffic circles differ from roundabouts?
cards.back: Roundabouts are generally larger than traffic circles but work the same way. Traffic circles are designed for residential streets where trucks and buses don't usually travel — if you're driving a large truck or bus through one, encroaching onto the median is okay to get through.

cards.front: What is a truck apron?
cards.back: Traffic circles and roundabouts often have a truck apron around the edge of the island in the middle. Large vehicles may need to drive over the apron in order to get through.

cards.front: When exiting a roundabout, what should you do with your signal?
cards.back: Signal "right" in advance of your exit location.

cards.front: List the tips for reducing your risk of a backing-up crash.
cards.back: Avoid backing up whenever possible; plan ahead to minimize the distance; be certain the area is clear; use a guide whenever possible (otherwise walk completely around the vehicle, repeating every vehicle length); sound your horn at least once every vehicle length; back out of traffic rather than into traffic.

cards.front: Where should you position a guide when backing up?
cards.back: Where the guide has a clear, continuous view of the backing path your vehicle will follow, and where you can see the guide throughout the manoeuvre.

cards.front: How does hood length affect a large vehicle's blind spots?
cards.back: There's an area immediately in front of the vehicle where you can't see anything — the longer the hood, the longer the blind spot. The high seat position can also hide a car or pedestrian alongside, particularly on the passenger side.

cards.front: Which lanes should you drive in on a freeway?
cards.back: The far right or centre lane, leaving the left lane for higher-speed traffic and passing vehicles. On a multi-lane divided highway, a right-hand lane is best.

cards.front: What are upshifting and downshifting, and when is each done?
cards.back: Upshifting is shifting to a higher gear, done when you want to go faster. Downshifting is shifting to a lower gear, done as you slow down. Both are performed with double-clutching, in slightly different ways.

cards.front: What is lugging?
cards.back: Lugging occurs when the engine is operated below peak torque for any length of time.

cards.front: Give an example of progressive shifting r.p.m. recommendations.
cards.back: The r.p.m. you shift at becomes higher as you select higher gears — for example, a manufacturer may recommend shifting from first to second gear at 1,200 r.p.m. and from fifth to sixth gear at 1,350 r.p.m.

cards.front: How should you respond when another driver wants to pass you?
cards.back: Help them pass safely: reduce your speed and give them room. But don't direct other drivers to pass — you may be encouraging a pass they can't complete safely.

cards.front: What gear should the transmission be placed in when parking?
cards.back: Lowest forward gear if parked facing uphill, reverse gear if facing downhill, or park with an automatic transmission. If the vehicle has main and auxiliary transmissions, place both in gear; a two-speed axle must be in low range.

cards.front: Which way do you turn the wheels when parking a tractor-trailer combination on an uphill?
cards.back: With or without a curb, always turn the wheels to the left towards the centre of the road. On a downgrade, any vehicle's wheels always turn right towards the edge of the roadway.

cards.front: What makes a railway crossing a controlled crossing?
cards.back: A controlled crossing has a flag person, stop sign, crossing gate, or an electric or mechanical signalling device. All vehicles must stop at controlled crossings if signalled to do so, and you must never cross if a crossing gate is down.

cards.front: How close to a railway crossing may you park?
cards.back: Don't park any vehicle within 15 m of the nearest rail of a railway crossing.

cards.front: Why are humpback railway crossings dangerous for low-clearance vehicles?
cards.back: Low bed trailers may hang up on the crossing surface or the rails, and low-hanging trailer appliances such as dolly wheels and tool boxes may catch on the rail.

cards.front: Why can you overrun your headlights at night even at legal speed?
cards.back: Most headlights illuminate the highway for only 100 m on high beam and less on low beam, but a large, loaded truck travelling at 80 km/h can take more than 100 m to stop — further than your high beams let you see. Slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see.

cards.front: When and how should you check tire pressure?
cards.back: Check and adjust tire pressure when the tires are cool, using a tire pressure gauge. A tire with correct pressure when cool generates a normal amount of heat in use. Reducing pressure when warm may upset the cooling balance and cause more heat.

cards.front: When is a tire defective under the tread-damage and tread-depth rules?
cards.back: Tread damage (cuts, cracks, snags) longer than 2.5 cm (1 in) and deep enough to expose the ply cords; less than 3 mm of tread on a front tire or 1.6 mm on a rear tire (vehicles with GVW of 5,500 kg or more); less than 1.6 mm on a trailer tire; less than 3.5 mm on a winter tire.

cards.front: Can radial and bias-ply tires be mixed on a vehicle?
cards.back: They can be mixed on the same vehicle but not on the same axle (and mixing isn't a recommended practice). After changing a tire, stop after a short while and check the wheel nuts are tight — always use a torque wrench.

cards.front: What braking systems must every motor vehicle have?
cards.back: At least two separate braking systems, one of which must be mechanical — for example a ratchet and pawl (notched wheel) or spring brake mechanism. If the foot (primary) brakes fail, the driver must use the emergency (mechanical) brake, which takes more time and distance to stop.

cards.front: Which flashing light colours are allowed on which vehicles?
cards.back: Red flashing lights only on emergency vehicles; blue only on police vehicles; amber on construction vehicles, towing vehicles, attending tow cars, snow-removal and sanding equipment, pilot cars, and vehicles required by permit to use them. A permit from Commercial Vehicle Safety and Enforcement is needed before mounting amber flashing lights.

cards.front: Which commercial vehicles must carry approved warning devices for use when disabled?
cards.back: All vehicles with a seating capacity of more than 10 passengers, all commercial vehicles with an overall width of more than 2.3 m, and all commercial vehicles with a load width of more than 2.3 m. Parked in the dark, they must put out a minimum of two warning devices.

cards.front: How far must you sit from the steering wheel airbag, and how should a head restraint be adjusted?
cards.back: Allow at least 25 cm (10 in) between your breastbone and the airbag unit. Adjust the head restraint so its top is at least as high as the top of your head and less than 10 cm from the back of your head.

cards.front: What electronic devices may a non-GLP commercial driver use while driving?
cards.back: Hands-free cellphones and devices that require touching only a single button (in a fixed and secure location) to activate or deactivate, pre-programmed or voice-activated GPS, two-way radios and mobile data terminals. Calling 9-1-1 to report an emergency is exempt from the restrictions.

cards.front: What can B.C.'s drinking and driving penalties cost you, even for a first offence?
cards.back: Penalties can add up to $600 to over $4,000 even the first time you're caught, plus time off the road. A Criminal Code conviction for driving while impaired, with a BAC over .08, or for refusing to provide a sample brings a fine of $1,000 and up, driving prohibitions and possible jail — with penalties becoming more severe for repeat offences.

cards.front: What should you do about fatigue on long trips?
cards.back: There's no safe substitute for proper rest or sleep — stay-awake tablets don't reduce mental fatigue. If you rely on stimulants like coffee or have trouble sleeping, pull over in a safe location and sleep. Follow the National Safety Code hours of service regulations and get enough sleep every 24 hours.

cards.front: What fire precautions apply when refuelling?
cards.back: Shut off the engine, keep the fuel hose nozzle in contact with the filler pipe at all times to ground the connection (connect the ground strap if there is one), and don't smoke in garages or near fuelling areas.

cards.front: How do you fight a fire under the hood, and why can't you use water on gasoline or oil fires?
cards.back: Direct the extinguisher from underneath the vehicle or through the radiator — don't open the hood. Water spreads gasoline and oil fires; use an appropriate extinguisher, sand or dirt to smother them. Fight fires with the wind at your back and keep some extinguishing fuel in reserve for flare-ups.

cards.front: How should you adjust your driving for ice, sleet or snow?
cards.back: Get the feel of the road when you start out — at a slow speed, test the steering and brakes for control. Reduce speed to suit conditions and put on chains if necessary. Apply light pressure to the brake and avoid quick or erratic steering movements. Keep windows clear inside and out, and stay alert for hazards like ice patches, bridge surfaces, snow plows and graders.

cards.front: With disk wheels, what problems mean you must not drive the vehicle?
cards.back: Loose or missing lug nuts, stripped studs, or cracks in the rim. Also investigate metal or paint flakes around the nuts (may indicate wheel movement) and oil or grease leaks from the hub. Rust streaks on the rim may indicate a loose lug nut or cracks in the rim.

cards.front: What should a driver do before entering a narrow bridge from a curved approach?
cards.back: Be familiar with the amount of off track your vehicle displays, and use that information to adjust your speed and approach to the curve so you can enter the bridge safely.

cards.front: What precautions apply when you can't make a right turn without swinging into another lane?
cards.back: You may need to turn wide as you complete the turn. If you must cross into the oncoming lane, watch for vehicles coming toward you and give them room to pass by or stop. Don't back up for them — you might hit someone behind you. It's your responsibility to be certain you can move safely.

cards.front: What are the two main categories of fire extinguishers?
cards.back: Multi-purpose dry chemical extinguishers and carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguishers. Dry chemical extinguishers are easier and safer to use, but CO2 extinguishers are more effective — though CO2 must never be used in an enclosed space.

questions.q: Which vehicles should use the two-second rule for following distance?
choices: Buses, trucks and truck-tractors with semi-trailers
Taxis, limousines, ride-hailing vehicles, ambulances and vans
Only motorcycles and passenger cars
Vehicles carrying dangerous goods
questions.explanation: Drivers of passenger cars and light trucks — including taxis, limousines, ride-hailing vehicles, ambulances and vans — should use the two-second rule. Heavy vehicles need at least five seconds.

questions.q: What minimum following distance should you keep when driving a bus, truck or other heavy vehicle?
choices: Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds
Five seconds
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles need more time and distance to stop, so keep at least a five-second following distance, and increase it when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.q: When driving a large commercial vehicle on a highway, how much space should you leave between your vehicle and other large commercial vehicles?
choices: At least 60 m (200 ft)
At least 30 m (100 ft)
At least 15 m (50 ft)
At least 100 m (330 ft)
questions.explanation: The guide says to leave at least 60 m (200 ft) between your vehicle and other large commercial vehicles on a highway.

questions.q: Which vehicles should display a red triangle slow moving vehicle sign?
choices: Any vehicle parked at the roadside
Vehicles, machinery or combinations that travel at less than 40 km/h
All commercial vehicles over 5,500 kg GVW
Vehicles that travel at less than 60 km/h
questions.explanation: Vehicles, machinery or combinations of vehicles that travel at less than 40 km/h should display the sign. It must not go on stationary objects or on vehicles travelling faster than 40 km/h.

questions.q: What is the best way to deal with a tailgater?
choices: Brake sharply to warn them off
Speed up to increase the gap
Allow them to pass, and make your stops gradual
Turn on your four-way flashers and stop
questions.explanation: Tailgaters are easiest to deal with when they're in front of you, so allow them to pass. Gradual stops reduce the impact if a rear-end collision can't be prevented.

questions.q: What is a vehicle's danger zone?
choices: The blind spot directly behind the vehicle
The area of air turbulence around the vehicle
The space other drivers should leave when passing
The section of road the vehicle travels through before it can stop
questions.explanation: The danger zone is the section of road a vehicle travels through before it can stop — it's physically impossible to stop in time to avoid a collision with anything in it. It grows with speed and poor road conditions.

questions.q: What should you do as soon as you see a potential hazard in your danger zone?
choices: Remove your foot from the accelerator and put it lightly on the brake pedal
Sound your horn and change lanes
Apply the brakes hard immediately
Downshift to a lower gear
questions.explanation: Covering the brake reduces your reaction time and slows your speed, helping you apply the brakes sooner and giving you a better chance of stopping before the crosswalk.

questions.q: In a turn, how does the wheel on the inside of the curve behave compared to the outside wheel?
choices: It turns less sharply and has a longer turning radius
It pivots more sharply and has a shorter turning radius
It follows exactly the same path as the outside wheel
It lifts slightly off the road surface
questions.explanation: The wheel on the inside of the curve must pivot more sharply to travel on the shorter radius than the wheel on the outside of the turn.

questions.q: What is "off track"?
choices: The tendency of a vehicle to continue in a straight line in a curve
The sideways slide of a trailer during hard braking
The difference between the path of the front wheels and the path of the rear wheels
The distance a vehicle travels after the brakes are applied
questions.explanation: When a vehicle moves around a curve, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels; that difference is called off track.

questions.q: Which of the following increases the amount of off track?
choices: A shorter wheelbase
Mounting the fifth wheel farther forward
A shorter draw bar
A longer wheelbase, longer draw bar or a fifth wheel mounted farther back
questions.explanation: The longer the wheelbase, and the longer the draw bar or the farther back the fifth wheel is mounted, the greater the amount of off track.

questions.q: When curving to the right, where should you keep your front wheels?
choices: Close to the centre line
Close to the right edge of the pavement
In the middle of your lane
On the pavement shoulder
questions.explanation: Keeping the front wheels close to the centre line prevents your rear wheels from dropping off the pavement or going onto the shoulder.

questions.q: How should you handle your speed in a curve?
choices: Brake steadily all the way through the curve
Reduce speed before entering, then apply gradual power in the curve
Accelerate into the curve to maintain traction
Coast through the curve in neutral
questions.explanation: Enter each curve at a speed that doesn't require braking and allows you to apply gradual power in the curve. Braking in a curve can cause a skid, rollover or jackknife.

questions.q: What is the most dangerous point in a right turn with a tractor and semi-trailer?
choices: Just before you start turning the steering wheel
When the trailer has finished the turn but the tractor hasn't
When both units are straight in the new lane
When the tractor has made the turn but the trailer hasn't
questions.explanation: At that point the right rear-view mirror is turned so that it's almost useless, so you can't see smaller vehicles, cyclists or pedestrians on your right side.

questions.q: When making a sharp right turn with a forward-control vehicle such as a bus, how far from the curb should you position the vehicle on the approach?
choices: As close to the curb as possible
Three to four metres
One to two metres
At least five metres
questions.explanation: Position the vehicle one to two metres from the curb, drive straight until the side street's curb line is visible through the front entrance door, then enter the turn at a low speed.

questions.q: If there are two left-turning lanes, which one should you turn from in a large commercial vehicle?
choices: The right-hand turn lane
The left-hand turn lane
Either lane, whichever is empty
Neither — large vehicles must turn right instead
questions.explanation: The right-hand turn lane will better accommodate your vehicle's off tracking.

questions.q: If another vehicle arrives at a traffic circle at the same time as you, what should you do?
choices: Proceed first because you're the larger vehicle
Yield to the vehicle on your right
Yield to the vehicle on your left
Both vehicles stop and wait for a signal
questions.explanation: Yield to any traffic already in the circle, and if another vehicle arrives at the same time as you, yield to the vehicle on your right.

questions.q: Is it acceptable to drive onto the median when taking a large truck or bus through a traffic circle?
choices: No, encroaching on the median is always illegal
Only when escorted by a pilot car
Yes, encroaching onto the median is okay to get through
Only at night when traffic is light
questions.explanation: Traffic circles are designed for residential streets where trucks and buses don't usually travel, so encroaching onto the median is okay for a large truck or bus to get through.

questions.q: Why might a large commercial vehicle need to take up more than one lane in a multi-lane roundabout?
choices: To block other vehicles from passing
Because roundabout lanes are reserved for trucks
To exit without signalling
Because of the vehicle's off track
questions.explanation: Due to the vehicle's off track you may need to take up more than one lane, so make sure there are no vehicles in the lane beside you.

questions.q: What causes most crashes that involve a backing-up vehicle?
choices: Drivers who didn't see something they should have
Mechanical failure of the brakes
Guides giving wrong directions
Backing up too slowly
questions.explanation: Most backing-up crashes are caused by drivers who didn't see something they should've, which is why you must make certain the way is clear — checking several times if necessary.

questions.q: If you must back up without a guide, what should you do before starting?
choices: Rely on your convex mirrors to check behind
Get out and walk completely around the vehicle, repeating every vehicle length
Back up quickly to minimize time in reverse
Turn on your four-way flashers and reverse in one long move
questions.explanation: Walk completely around the vehicle before backing and repeat this every vehicle length. Sound your horn at least once every vehicle length, and prefer a series of short backing manoeuvres over one long one.

questions.q: When choosing how to approach a loading area, which is the safer practice?
choices: Drive straight in so you can back into traffic when leaving
Back into the blind side to save time
Back out of traffic into the area, so you can drive forward to leave
Park parallel to traffic and back across both lanes
questions.explanation: It's easier and safer to back out of traffic than into traffic, and to back into the view side rather than the blind side, so you can see the area you're backing into.

questions.q: How do convex or spot mirrors affect what you see?
choices: They make things look larger and closer than they are
They show the true size and distance of objects
They only work at night
They make things look smaller and farther away than they actually are
questions.explanation: Convex or spot mirrors make things look smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.q: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing red or blue lights and a siren?
choices: Drive parallel to and as close as possible to the nearest edge or curb, stop clear of any intersection, and remain stopped until it has passed
Speed up and clear the area as quickly as possible
Stop immediately wherever you are, including in the intersection
Slow to 40 km/h and continue driving
questions.explanation: Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the nearest edge, stopping clear of any intersection, and staying stopped until the emergency vehicle passes. Don't assume there's only one emergency vehicle.

questions.q: You're approaching a stopped vehicle displaying flashing lights on a road where the speed limit is 80 km/h or more. What is your maximum speed?
choices: 40 km/h
70 km/h
60 km/h
80 km/h
questions.explanation: You must drive no faster than 70 km/h if the speed limit is 80 km/h or more, and no faster than 40 km/h if the speed limit is less than 80 km/h.

questions.q: You're in the lane nearest a stopped vehicle displaying flashing lights. Besides slowing down, what must you do?
choices: Sound your horn as you pass
Stop completely until the vehicle leaves
Change lanes to provide safe space margins, if it is safe to do so
Turn on your high beams
questions.explanation: If you're in the lane nearest the stopped vehicle, you must also change lanes to provide safe space margins if it's safe. Failing to slow down and/or change lanes may result in a traffic violation and penalty points.

questions.q: What is double-clutching?
choices: Using two clutch pedals in a heavy vehicle
Riding the clutch while braking
Skipping gears to accelerate faster
Depressing the clutch pedal twice in the process of moving from one gear to another
questions.explanation: Double-clutching means depressing the clutch pedal twice while moving between gears. It's essential because most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions don't have synchromesh gears.

questions.q: What is the normal operating r.p.m. range of an engine?
choices: Between the engine's peak torque and peak horsepower
Between idle and peak torque
Above peak horsepower
Whatever range the governor prevents
questions.explanation: The vehicle should be operated between the engine's peak torque and peak horsepower — peak torque is found at a lower engine speed than peak horsepower.

questions.q: What does an engine governor do?
choices: Increases horsepower at high altitude
Controls the amount of fuel going to the engine and regulates engine speed
Automatically shifts the transmission
Disengages the clutch during braking
questions.explanation: A governor controls the fuel going to the engine and regulates engine speed, and it lets you start a vehicle on level ground and on grades without using the throttle. Small vehicles don't have governors.

questions.q: A small vehicle keeps riding in your truck's area of air turbulence. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to move away from it
Sound your horn until it moves
Slow down until it's out of the turbulence area
Change lanes toward it to warn the driver
questions.explanation: Air turbulence from a large vehicle can force smaller road users off a narrow roadway or draw them into the side of your vehicle — and can cause cyclists to lose control — so slow down until they're out of it.

questions.q: When parking a single-unit vehicle facing uphill where there is a curb, which way should you turn the wheels?
choices: Straight ahead
To the right, towards the edge of the roadway
It doesn't matter if the parking brake is set
To the left, towards the centre of the road
questions.explanation: A single-unit vehicle parked uphill with a curb should have its wheels turned left towards the centre of the road; uphill with no curb, turn them right towards the edge.

questions.q: When parking any vehicle on a downgrade, which way should the wheels be turned?
choices: Always to the right, towards the edge of the roadway
Always to the left, towards the centre of the road
Left with a curb, right without a curb
Wheels should stay straight on a downgrade
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, always turn the wheels to the right towards the edge of the roadway, and block the wheels of any large vehicle parked on even a slight grade.

questions.q: Why should you never use a trailer hand valve to hold an unattended unit?
choices: It wears out the brake linings
Over time the air may drain away and the brakes may release
It locks only the tractor brakes
It causes the spring brakes to overheat
questions.explanation: Air pressure may bleed down over time, causing the brakes to release and the vehicle to run away. If a trailer has no spring brakes, apply the trailer brakes and block the wheels.

questions.q: What is a "stale" green light?
choices: A light that has just turned green
A green light that is malfunctioning
A light that's been the same colour for some time and could change before you reach the intersection
A flashing green light at a pedestrian crossing
questions.explanation: A stale light has been the same colour for some time, meaning it could change before you reach the intersection — be prepared to stop.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed in a lane or alley unless otherwise posted?
choices: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
20 km/h
questions.explanation: The maximum speed in a lane or alley is 20 km/h unless otherwise posted. When driving from an alley onto a highway, stop before crossing the sidewalk and yield to pedestrians and vehicles.

questions.q: How far from a railway crossing should you stop when required to stop?
choices: Five to 15 m from the crossing
One to three metres from the crossing
20 to 30 m from the crossing
Immediately at the nearest rail
questions.explanation: Stop five to 15 m from the crossing, look both ways and listen (opening your window or bus door helps you hear), then move forward when safe without shifting gears while crossing.

questions.q: Which of the following vehicles is required to stop at all uncontrolled main railway crossings?
choices: All commercial vehicles over 5,500 kg GVW
A vehicle transporting liquefied petroleum gas, whether empty or loaded
Any vehicle towing a trailer
All vehicles displaying amber flashing lights
questions.explanation: School buses carrying children, buses carrying passengers, vehicles transporting explosive, poisonous or flammable substances, and vehicles used to transport combustibles, corrosive liquids or liquefied petroleum gas (empty or loaded) must stop at all uncontrolled main railway crossings.

questions.q: Before crossing a railway line, how much time should the clear track give you to cross?
choices: At least 5 seconds
At least 30 seconds
At least 10 seconds — more if your vehicle requires it or you're crossing more than one track
At least 60 seconds
questions.explanation: Check that the track is clear far enough to give you at least 10 seconds to cross — more if your vehicle requires it or if you're crossing more than one track at a time.

questions.q: What must you avoid doing while driving across railway tracks?
choices: Using your four-way flashers
Looking both ways
Sounding your horn
Shifting gears
questions.explanation: You must not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks, and before starting across, be certain there's room for your vehicle on the other side — stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous.

questions.q: A large animal is directly ahead and you can't stop in time. What does the guide recommend?
choices: Brake firmly, steer to strike the animal at an angle, and let up on the brake just before hitting it
Slam on the brakes and hold them to the point of impact
Swerve sharply into the oncoming lane
Accelerate to push the animal clear
questions.explanation: Braking firmly and steering to strike at an angle, then letting up on the brake just before impact, causes the front of your vehicle to rise and reduces the chance the animal will come through the windshield.

questions.q: At night, how far before meeting or following another vehicle must you switch from high beam to low beam?
choices: At least 60 m away
At least 150 m away
At least 100 m away
At least 300 m away
questions.explanation: Switch from high beam to low beam at least 150 m away from any vehicle you're approaching or following to reduce glare on other drivers' eyes.

questions.q: What is a major cause of failure in recapped (retread) tires?
choices: Overinflation
Driving in cold weather
Underinflation
Using a torque wrench on the wheel nuts
questions.explanation: Underinflation is a major cause of recapped tire failure — underinflated tires flex more, and more flexing means more heat, risking tire damage or a blowout.

questions.q: Where does an overinflated tire show excess wear?
choices: On the outer edges of the tread
On the sidewalls
Evenly across the whole tread
In the centre part of the tread
questions.explanation: Overinflation causes excess wear in the centre of the tread and reduces tread contact with the road, which means less traction. Underinflation wears the outer edges and increases the chance of hydroplaning.

questions.q: On a vehicle with a GVW of 5,500 kg or more, a front tire is defective when its tread depth is less than:
choices: 3 mm (1/8 in)
2.5 cm (1 in)
questions.explanation: A tire is defective with less than 3 mm (1/8 in) of tread on a front tire or 1.6 mm (1/16 in) on a rear tire when used on a vehicle with a GVW of 5,500 kg or more.

questions.q: What must all vehicles using air or vacuum brakes be equipped with?
choices: Automatic traction control
Warning devices that alert the driver if the air-pressure or vacuum system fails
A secondary hydraulic braking circuit
An engine retarder
questions.explanation: All vehicles using air or vacuum brakes must have warning devices to warn the driver of an air-pressure or vacuum system failure.

questions.q: If your commercial vehicle becomes disabled at the roadside, where should you place your warning devices?
choices: 10 m ahead and 10 m behind the vehicle
Only directly behind the vehicle
Approximately 30 m ahead and 30 m behind the vehicle
50 m behind the vehicle only
questions.explanation: Move the vehicle as far off the travelled portion of the highway as possible and place warning devices approximately 30 m ahead and 30 m behind it — placing additional devices even further away is good practice.

questions.q: By how much does correct use of a lap and shoulder belt system reduce the likelihood of death in a crash?
choices: 25 per cent
10 per cent
90 per cent
50 per cent
questions.explanation: It's estimated that correct use of a lap and shoulder belt system reduces the likelihood of death in a motor vehicle crash by 50 per cent.

questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous to drivers?
choices: It's odourless, colourless, tasteless and difficult to detect
It has a strong smell that causes distraction
It only forms in diesel engines
It makes the engine overheat
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is odourless, colourless, tasteless and difficult to detect, and it's in the exhaust of every motor vehicle. It can make you dizzy or drowsy, cause you to pass out, and kill you.

questions.q: Which drivers are restricted from using even hands-free electronic devices while driving?
choices: All commercial drivers
Drivers in B.C.'s Graduated Licensing Program (GLP)
Drivers over 65 years of age
Drivers of vehicles with air brakes
questions.explanation: All B.C. drivers are prohibited from using hand-held electronic devices while driving, and GLP drivers are also restricted from operating hands-free devices. Calling 9-1-1 to report an emergency is the exception.

questions.q: For how long can police immediately impound a vehicle whose driver is caught excessive speeding or driving while prohibited?
choices: 24 hours
Three days
Seven days, which could escalate to 30 or 60 days for repeat offenders
90 days for a first offence
questions.explanation: Police can immediately impound the vehicle for seven days, escalating to 30 or 60 days for repeat offenders. The owner must pay the towing and storage fees to get the vehicle back.

questions.q: Excessive speeding, an offence that can lead to vehicle impoundment, means driving:
choices: 10 km/h or more over the posted limit
20 km/h or more over the posted limit
30 km/h or more over the posted limit
40 km/h or more over the posted limit
questions.explanation: Excessive speeding is 40 km/h or more over the posted limit. Impoundment also applies to driving while unlicensed, suspended or prohibited, and street racing or stunt driving.

questions.q: Why should a CO2 fire extinguisher never be used in an enclosed space?
choices: You could smother yourself, and it could blister your skin
It's ineffective on any fire indoors
It produces toxic smoke when discharged
It can explode in confined areas
questions.explanation: CO2 extinguishers are extremely effective, but in a confined space you could smother yourself, and the discharge could also blister your skin.

questions.q: A dry chemical fire extinguisher cylinder marked "BC" can put out which fires?
choices: Only paper and cloth fires
Grease, oil, gasoline and electrical fires
Only fires in enclosed spaces
Any fire, including burning metals
questions.explanation: A BC-marked extinguisher handles grease, oil, gasoline and electrical fires; an ABC-marked extinguisher will also put out Class A fires such as paper and cloth.

questions.q: How many fire extinguishers must a vehicle transporting explosives carry?
choices: None, if it carries flares instead
One
Two
Four
questions.explanation: Vehicles transporting explosives must carry two fire extinguishers.

questions.q: Which of the following vehicles must carry one fire extinguisher?
choices: All commercial vehicles wider than 2.3 m
All vehicles equipped with air brakes
All vehicles that transport combustible liquids only
All school buses, with extinguishers meeting CSA Standard D250
questions.explanation: One fire extinguisher must be carried on limited passenger vehicles with an authorized seating capacity of more than 10, all public passenger vehicles, and all school buses (meeting CSA Standard D250).
